```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chang_2024_mavacamten"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chang_2024_mavacamten"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13197> (open access; the final
  parameter estimates are in Supplementary Table S5)
* Corroborating source: the FDA clinical pharmacology review of NDA 214998
  (Table 4-2, "Applicant's final model run117"),
  <https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214998Orig1s000ClinPharmR.pdf>

Mavacamten is an oral cardiac myosin inhibitor for symptomatic obstructive
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Chang 2024 pooled 12 studies into a linear
two-compartment model with first-order absorption after a lag time. Apparent
clearance depends on body weight, CYP2C19 phenotype, eGFR, health status, sex
and concomitant omeprazole or esomeprazole; absorption rate, lag time and
relative bioavailability depend on the dose given, the formulation, food status
(healthy participants only) and sex.

# Population

The analysis set held 9244 plasma concentrations from 497 adults: 192 healthy
participants in seven phase 1 studies, 54 patients with nonobstructive HCM
(MAVERICK-HCM) and 251 patients with obstructive HCM (PIONEER-HCM,
EXPLORER-HCM and the MAVA-LTE extension) (Chang 2024 Table 1). Mean age was
49.4 years (range 18-82), mean body weight 81.1 kg (SD 16.9), 40.2% were women,
79.5% White, 12.5% Asian and 5.0% Black, and mean eGFR was 94.5
mL/min/1.73 m^2 (range 29.5-148) (Table 2). CYP2C19 phenotype was normal
metabolizer (`*1/*1`) in 39.8%, `*1/*2`-type intermediate in 17.9%, rapid
(`*1/*17`) in 19.1%, `*2/*17` in 4.6%, poor in 3.4%, ultrarapid (`*17/*17`) in
3.2% and missing in 11.9%. Single doses ranged from 1 to 48 mg and multiple
doses from 2 to 25 mg/day.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Chang_2024_mavacamten")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. Values
come from Chang 2024 Supplementary Table S5; Table 3 repeats the structural
parameters and the FDA review's Table 4-2 repeats every value.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL/F) | log(0.914 L/h) | Table S5, Table 3 |
| `lvc` (V2/F) | log(6.63 L) | Table S5, Table 3 |
| `lvp` (V3/F) | log(252 L) | Table S5, Table 3 |
| `lq` (Q/F) | log(16.3 L/h) | Table S5, Table 3 |
| `lka` (KA) | log(0.301 1/h) | Table S5, Table 3 |
| `ltlag` (ALAG1) | log(0.192 h) | Table S5, Table 3 |
| `lfdepot` (F) | fixed log(1) | Table S5, Table 3 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75 (fixed) | Table S5 'Body weight-CLx/F'; Methods |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | 0.813 | Table S5 'Body weight-Vx/F' |
| `e_cyp2c19_pm_cl`, `_im_cl`, `_rm_cl`, `_um_cl`, `_missing_cl` | -0.722, -0.331, -0.00218, 0.253, -0.14 | Table S5 |
| `e_healthy_cl` | 0.272 | Table S5 'Healthy individual-CL/F' |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.205 | Table S5 'eGFR-CL/F' |
| `e_esomeprazole_cl`, `e_omeprazole_cl` | -0.421, -0.332 | Table S5 |
| `e_sexf_cl`, `e_sexf_f` | 0.273, 0.0945 | Table S5 'Female sex-CL/F', 'Female sex-F' |
| `e_form_solution_ka`, `e_form_solution_f` | 0.681, -0.194 | Table S5 |
| `e_healthy_fast_ka` | 0.873 | Table S5 'Healthy individual, fasted-KA' |
| `e_dose_ka`, `e_dose_tlag`, `e_dose_f` | -0.135, -0.087, 0.0777 | Table S5 |
| `e_healthy_fast_f`, `e_healthy_fed_f` | -0.314, -0.433 | Table S5 |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc`, `etalvp` block | CV 57.2%, 217%, 22.9%; r = -0.021, 0.576, 0.0307 | Table S5 random effects |
| `etalka`, `etalq`, `etaruv` | CV 42.9%, 23.3%, 49.3% | Table S5 random effects |
| `expSd`, `expSdMyk461014` | sqrt(0.0292), sqrt(0.478) | Table S5 'EP', 'EP14' |
| Continuous covariates: `P = TVP * (X / M)^theta` | M = 84 kg, 95 mL/min/1.73 m^2, 5 mg | Figure S2; reference participant (Methods, Figure 1) |
| Categorical covariates: `P = TVP * (1 + theta)^X` | n/a | Figure S2 |
| Two-compartment ODEs with lag and first-order absorption | n/a | Results 'Base structural model' |
| Residual error: log-normal, IIV on its magnitude | n/a | Results 'Covariate analysis'; Table S5 |

# Covariate effects (Figure 1)

Figure 1 of Chang 2024 prints the effect of each covariate on each parameter as
a percentage of the reference value. Recomputing them from the packaged
parameters checks both the transcription and the two covariate forms of Figure
S2: a power function of `X / M` for continuous covariates and `(1 + theta)^X`
for categorical ones.

```{r figure-1}
mod <- readModelDb("Chang_2024_mavacamten")
th <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta

fig1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter, ~covariate,                         ~computed,                                            ~published,
  "ALAG1",    "Dose 1 mg vs 5 mg",                 100 * (1 / 5)^th[["e_dose_tlag"]],                     115,
  "ALAG1",    "Dose 25 mg vs 5 mg",                100 * (25 / 5)^th[["e_dose_tlag"]],                    86.9,
  "CL/F",     "WT 58 kg vs 84 kg",                 100 * (58 / 84)^th[["e_wt_cl"]],                       75.7,
  "CL/F",     "WT 108 kg vs 84 kg",                100 * (108 / 84)^th[["e_wt_cl"]],                      121,
  "CL/F",     "Omeprazole",                        100 * (1 + th[["e_omeprazole_cl"]]),                   66.8,
  "CL/F",     "Healthy participant",               100 * (1 + th[["e_healthy_cl"]]),                      127,
  "CL/F",     "Female",                            100 * (1 + th[["e_sexf_cl"]]),                         127,
  "CL/F",     "Esomeprazole",                      100 * (1 + th[["e_esomeprazole_cl"]]),                 57.9,
  "CL/F",     "eGFR 60 vs 95",                     100 * (60 / 95)^th[["e_crcl_cl"]],                     91.0,
  "CL/F",     "eGFR 127 vs 95",                    100 * (127 / 95)^th[["e_crcl_cl"]],                    106,
  "CL/F",     "CYP2C19 missing",                   100 * (1 + th[["e_cyp2c19_missing_cl"]]),              86.0,
  "CL/F",     "CYP2C19 UM",                        100 * (1 + th[["e_cyp2c19_um_cl"]]),                   125,
  "CL/F",     "CYP2C19 RM",                        100 * (1 + th[["e_cyp2c19_rm_cl"]]),                   99.8,
  "CL/F",     "CYP2C19 PM",                        100 * (1 + th[["e_cyp2c19_pm_cl"]]),                   27.8,
  "CL/F",     "CYP2C19 IM",                        100 * (1 + th[["e_cyp2c19_im_cl"]]),                   66.9,
  "F",        "Healthy, fed",                      100 * (1 + th[["e_healthy_fed_f"]]),                   56.7,
  "F",        "Dose 1 mg vs 5 mg",                 100 * (1 / 5)^th[["e_dose_f"]],                        88.2,
  "F",        "Dose 25 mg vs 5 mg",                100 * (25 / 5)^th[["e_dose_f"]],                       113,
  "F",        "Healthy, fasted",                   100 * (1 + th[["e_healthy_fast_f"]]),                  68.6,
  "F",        "Oral solution",                     100 * (1 + th[["e_form_solution_f"]]),                 80.6,
  "F",        "Female",                            100 * (1 + th[["e_sexf_f"]]),                          109,
  "KA",       "Dose 1 mg vs 5 mg",                 100 * (1 / 5)^th[["e_dose_ka"]],                       124,
  "KA",       "Dose 25 mg vs 5 mg",                100 * (25 / 5)^th[["e_dose_ka"]],                      80.4,
  "KA",       "Healthy, fasted",                   100 * (1 + th[["e_healthy_fast_ka"]]),                 187,
  "KA",       "Oral solution",                     100 * (1 + th[["e_form_solution_ka"]]),                168,
  "Q/F",      "WT 58 kg vs 84 kg",                 100 * (58 / 84)^th[["e_wt_cl"]],                       75.7,
  "Q/F",      "WT 108 kg vs 84 kg",                100 * (108 / 84)^th[["e_wt_cl"]],                      121,
  "V2/F",     "WT 58 kg vs 84 kg",                 100 * (58 / 84)^th[["e_wt_vc_vp"]],                    74.0,
  "V2/F",     "WT 108 kg vs 84 kg",                100 * (108 / 84)^th[["e_wt_vc_vp"]],                   123
) |>
  mutate(difference = computed - published)

fig1 |>
  mutate(computed = signif(computed, 3), difference = round(difference, 2)) |>
  rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter,
    "Covariate" = covariate,
    "Packaged model (% of reference)" = computed,
    "Figure 1 (% of reference)" = published,
    "Difference (points)" = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Covariate effects recomputed from the packaged parameters against Chang 2024 Figure 1.")

# Figure 1 prints three significant figures, so a correct transcription agrees
# to within rounding (0.5 points at 100-187%); a wrong sign or a wrong
# covariate form moves a row by several points.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig1$difference) < 0.6))
```

Every row agrees to the printed precision. The V3/F row of Figure 1 is not in
the table: it prints the same values as Q/F (75.7% and 121%, with a zero-width
interval), which is what an exponent of 0.75 gives, whereas Table S5 and the
FDA review both list one estimated exponent of 0.813 for V2/F and V3/F. The
model follows the two tables (see Assumptions and deviations).

# Steady-state exposure by covariate (Figure 2)

Figure 2 of Chang 2024 shows the median and 5th-95th percentiles of
steady-state Cavg, Ctrough and Cmax for a reference participant (male patient
with obstructive HCM, 84 kg, CYP2C19 normal metabolizer, eGFR 95
mL/min/1.73 m^2, 5 mg once daily, no PPI) and for participants who differ from
it in one covariate. The authors simulated 500 participants per scenario; 200
are simulated here.

```{r cohort}
scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                    ~WT, ~CRCL, ~dose, ~SEXF, ~DIS_HEALTHY, ~CONMED_ESOMEPRAZOLE, ~CONMED_OMEPRAZOLE, ~CYP2C19_UM, ~CYP2C19_RM, ~CYP2C19_IM, ~CYP2C19_PM,
  "Reference",                   84,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "WT: 45 kg",                   45,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "WT: 65 kg",                   65,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "WT: 105 kg",                 105,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "WT: 140 kg",                 140,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "Healthy individual, fasted",  84,    95,   5,     0,     1,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "Female",                      84,    95,   5,     1,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "Esomeprazole",                84,    95,   5,     0,     0,            1,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "Omeprazole",                  84,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    1,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "eGFR: 45",                    84,    45,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "eGFR: 75",                    84,    75,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "Dose: 2.5 mg",                84,    95, 2.5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "Dose: 10 mg",                 84,    95,  10,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "Dose: 15 mg",                 84,    95,  15,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           0,
  "CYP2C19: UM",                 84,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  1,           0,           0,           0,
  "CYP2C19: RM",                 84,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           1,           0,           0,
  "CYP2C19: IM",                 84,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           1,           0,
  "CYP2C19: PM",                 84,    95,   5,     0,     0,            0,                    0,                  0,           0,           0,           1
) |>
  mutate(
    scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenario),
    FED = 0, FORM_SOLUTION = 0, CYP2C19_MISSING = 0, STUDY_MYK461014 = 0
  )

n_per_scenario <- 200L
obs_times <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24)

subjects <- scenarios |>
  slice(rep(seq_len(n()), each = n_per_scenario)) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))

# One steady-state dose (ss = 1, ii = 24 h) followed by a dosing interval of
# observations. The dose column comes after the event columns so rxode2 does not
# read DOSE_MAVACAMTEN_MG as the dose amount.
dose_rows <- subjects |>
  mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot", ss = 1L, ii = 24)
obs_rows <- subjects |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", ss = 0L, ii = 0)
events_ss <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  mutate(DOSE_MAVACAMTEN_MG = dose) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, ss, ii, everything(), -dose) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_ss[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241029)
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_ss, keep = c("scenario")) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## PKNCA over the steady-state dosing interval

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_ss |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, scenario)
nca_dose <- events_ss |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, scenario)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | scenario + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | scenario + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_ss <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  select(id, scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
```

At steady state the trough of a once-daily regimen is the end-of-interval
concentration, which over a dosing interval with a lag is the interval minimum,
so PKNCA `cmin` gives Ctrough.

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6}
nca_ss |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cav, cmin, cmax), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, c("cav", "cmin", "cmax"),
    c("Cavg,ss", "Ctrough,ss", "Cmax,ss"))) |>
  group_by(scenario, metric) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), Q50 = median(value), Q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Q50, y = factor(scenario, levels = rev(levels(scenario))))) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = Q05, xmax = Q95)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Concentration (ng/mL)", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Chang 2024: median and 5th-95th percentiles, 200 simulated participants per row.")
```

## Comparison against Figure 2

The medians of Figure 2 panel (a) were digitised by the maintainers from the
published figure (axis 0-2000 ng/mL over about 157 pixels, so roughly 13 ng/mL
per pixel). The table compares them with the simulated medians.

```{r nca-compare}
published_cav <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                     ~cav,
  "Reference",                    229,
  "WT: 45 kg",                    362,
  "WT: 65 kg",                    273,
  "WT: 105 kg",                   184,
  "WT: 140 kg",                   153,
  "Healthy individual, fasted",    83,
  "Female",                       210,
  "Esomeprazole",                 388,
  "Omeprazole",                   337,
  "eGFR: 45",                     261,
  "eGFR: 75",                     242,
  "Dose: 2.5 mg",                 102,
  "Dose: 10 mg",                  502,
  "Dose: 15 mg",                  795,
  "CYP2C19: UM",                  178,
  "CYP2C19: RM",                  229,
  "CYP2C19: IM",                  343,
  "CYP2C19: PM",                  808
) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = levels(scenarios$scenario)))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_cav,
  by = "scenario",
  params = "cav",
  units = c(cav = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. digitised Figure 2(a) median Cavg,ss. * differs from the figure by more than 20%.")
```


## Typical-value check

With the random effects removed, Cavg,ss for each scenario must equal
`F * dose / (CL/F * 24 h)`, written here from Table S5 values rather than from
the model file.

```{r typical}
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = events_ss |> filter(id %in% seq(1, nrow(subjects), by = n_per_scenario)),
  keep = c("scenario")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

typ <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(id, scenario) |>
  summarise(cav_sim = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2) / 24, .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(scenarios, by = "scenario") |>
  mutate(
    cl = 0.914 * (WT / 84)^0.75 * (CRCL / 95)^0.205 *
      (1 - 0.722)^CYP2C19_PM * (1 - 0.331)^CYP2C19_IM * (1 - 0.00218)^CYP2C19_RM *
      (1 + 0.253)^CYP2C19_UM * (1 + 0.272)^DIS_HEALTHY *
      (1 - 0.332)^CONMED_OMEPRAZOLE * (1 - 0.421)^CONMED_ESOMEPRAZOLE * (1 + 0.273)^SEXF,
    f = (dose / 5)^0.0777 * (1 - 0.314)^DIS_HEALTHY * (1 + 0.0945)^SEXF,
    cav_closed = 1000 * f * dose / (cl * 24),
    pct_diff = 100 * (cav_sim / cav_closed - 1)
  )

typ |>
  select(scenario, cav_closed, cav_sim, pct_diff) |>
  mutate(across(c(cav_closed, cav_sim), \(x) signif(x, 4)), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 2)) |>
  rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Closed form Cavg,ss (ng/mL)" = cav_closed,
    "Simulated Cavg,ss (ng/mL)" = cav_sim,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-participant Cavg,ss: simulation against the closed form.")

# Same parameters on both sides: the only difference is trapezoidal error over
# the 17-point grid, well under 1% for this slowly varying profile.
stopifnot(all(abs(typ$pct_diff) < 1))
```

The typical-value Cavg,ss for the reference participant is
`r signif(typ$cav_closed[typ$scenario == "Reference"], 3)` ng/mL, against
about 229 ng/mL read from Figure 2.

## Gate against Figure 2

The figure's medians come from 500 simulated participants per row, so each
carries about 4% sampling error on top of the digitising error. The
typical-participant Cavg,ss above is the population median of Cavg,ss (no
random effect enters F or the dose, and CL/F is log-normal), so it is compared
with the figure directly; the 200-subject simulated medians get a looser
envelope.

```{r figure-2-gate}
gate <- typ |>
  select(scenario, cav_closed) |>
  left_join(nca_ss |> group_by(scenario) |> summarise(sim = median(cav), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "scenario") |>
  left_join(published_cav, by = "scenario") |>
  mutate(
    closed_pct = 100 * (cav_closed / cav - 1),
    sim_pct = 100 * (sim / cav - 1)
  )

gate |>
  mutate(across(c(cav_closed, sim), \(x) signif(x, 3)), across(c(closed_pct, sim_pct), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "Typical Cavg,ss (ng/mL)" = cav_closed,
    "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = sim,
    "Figure 2(a) median (ng/mL)" = cav,
    "Typical vs figure (%)" = closed_pct,
    "Simulated vs figure (%)" = sim_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median Cavg,ss against the digitised Figure 2(a).")

# The healthy-fasted row is the known deviation discussed below.
ok <- gate |> filter(scenario != "Healthy individual, fasted")
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic: no simulation noise on the model side. Observed spread is
  # -6.7% to +5.9%, from the figure's own sampling and digitising error;
  # dropping or sign-flipping any CYP2C19 (other than RM), PPI, weight or sex
  # effect moves its row by more than 10%.
  abs(median(ok$closed_pct)) < 3,
  all(abs(ok$closed_pct) < 10),
  # Stochastic: a 200-subject median adds about 5% sampling error per row.
  abs(median(ok$sim_pct)) < 6,
  quantile(abs(ok$sim_pct), 0.9) < 20
)
```

# Single doses in healthy participants (Figure S1)

Supplementary Figure S1 shows mean concentrations after single oral-solution
doses of 1-48 mg in fasted healthy participants (study MYK-461-002). The plot
below simulates the same doses with the packaged model for a male healthy
participant of 72.7 kg (the healthy-cohort mean in Table 2), eGFR 106
mL/min/1.73 m^2, CYP2C19 normal metabolizer.

```{r figure-s1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5}
sad_doses <- c(1, 2, 6, 12, 24, 48)
sad_times <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, 168, 240, 336, 504, 672)
sad <- tidyr::expand_grid(dose = sad_doses, rep = seq_len(100)) |>
  mutate(id = seq_len(n()))
sad_events <- bind_rows(
  sad |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot"),
  sad |> tidyr::expand_grid(time = sad_times) |> mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  mutate(
    DOSE_MAVACAMTEN_MG = dose, WT = 72.7, CRCL = 106, SEXF = 0, DIS_HEALTHY = 1,
    FED = 0, FORM_SOLUTION = 1, CYP2C19_PM = 0, CYP2C19_IM = 0, CYP2C19_RM = 0,
    CYP2C19_UM = 0, CYP2C19_MISSING = 0, CONMED_OMEPRAZOLE = 0,
    CONMED_ESOMEPRAZOLE = 0, STUDY_MYK461014 = 0,
    treatment = paste(dose, "mg")
  ) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, everything(), -rep, -dose) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241030)
sim_sad <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = sad_events, keep = c("treatment")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, paste(sad_doses, "mg")))

sim_sad |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(mean_Cc = mean(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, mean_Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Mean mavacamten (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose",
    caption = "Compare with Supplementary Figure S1 of Chang 2024 (observed means, MYK-461-002).")
```

The simulated means rise and fall with the same shape as Figure S1 (a rapid
peak within about 1 h, a distribution phase over the first day and a terminal
phase lasting weeks). Figure S1 is a plot of observed means from six
participants per dose, which are not dose-proportional at the lowest doses, so
no numeric gate is placed on it. The level is informative all the same: at 48 h
the simulated mean after 48 mg is
`r signif(mean(sim_sad$Cc[sim_sad$time == 48 & sim_sad$treatment == "48 mg"]), 2)`
ng/mL, against about 95 ng/mL in Figure S1. These are fasted healthy
participants, so their exposure carries the healthy-fasted F and CL/F effects
of Table S5; the healthy-fasted ratio printed in Figure 2 (see below) would put
them about a third lower.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV.** Table S5 reports the random effects as CV% = 100 *
  sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1); the packaged variances are omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2).
  The FDA review's Table 4-2 reports the same model's eta standard deviations
  (53.2%, 131.9%, 22.6%, 41.1%, 23% and 46.6% for CL/F, V2/F, V3/F, KA, Q/F and
  the residual magnitude), which are the square roots of these variances to
  three figures. Covariances are r * omega_i * omega_j from the correlations
  in Table S5.
- **Residual error.** The data were log-transformed. The maintainers read
  Table S5 'EP' (0.0292) and 'EP14' (0.478, study MYK-461-014) as NONMEM SIGMA
  variances, so the log-scale SDs are 0.171 and 0.691. Read as SDs, 0.0292
  would be a 2.9% residual error for pooled phase 1-3 data with mainly trough
  sampling, which is implausibly small. The participant-level IIV on the
  residual magnitude (CV 49.3%) multiplies the SD, as an
  `EPS * EXP(ETA)` construction would. `STUDY_MYK461014` should be 0 for new
  simulations.
- **Covariate reference values.** Figure S2 centres continuous covariates on
  "the approximate median" without listing it; the maintainers used the
  reference participant's values (84 kg, eGFR 95 mL/min/1.73 m^2, 5 mg),
  which Table 3 calls the reference for the structural estimates and which
  reproduce every Figure 1 percentage above.
- **V3/F weight exponent.** Table S5 and the FDA review list a single
  estimated exponent 0.813 for "Vx/F" (V2/F and V3/F). Figure 1 prints the
  V3/F weight effect as 75.7% and 121% with a zero-width interval, the values
  of the fixed 0.75 exponent used for CL/F and Q/F. The model follows the two
  tables.
- **Food effect on KA.** The Results text says KA was faster under fed than
  under fasted conditions, but Table S5 (and the FDA review) give an effect of
  +87.3% on KA for healthy fasted participants and Figure 1 plots it as 187%
  of the reference; the fed-healthy KA effect was removed from the final model.
  The model follows the table and figure.
- **Food status in patients.** Food status was unknown for every patient
  record, so the fed and fasted effects on KA and F apply only when
  `DIS_HEALTHY = 1`; patients take the reference absorption whatever `FED`
  holds.
- **CYP2C19 groups.** The paper's IM effect was estimated in the `*1/*2`-type
  group (Figure 1, n = 89, printed as "EM" in Tables 2 and S2). The Results
  report no difference in CL/F between `*2/*17` and `*1/*2`, so `*2/*17`
  carriers (n = 23) are coded IM; Figure 1 does not say where they were
  placed. UM is `*17/*17` only and RM is `*1/*17`.
- **Dose covariate.** `DOSE_MAVACAMTEN_MG` is the amount of each
  administration (equal to the daily dose in the once-daily regimens that
  dominate the data). It must be set on dose records; the source carried each
  dose record's value forward to the following observations.
- **Figure 2 deviation.** The healthy-fasted row of Figure 2 is not
  reproduced. Its median Cavg,ss reads about 83 ng/mL (36% of the
  reference), but Table S5 gives F x 0.686 and CL/F x 1.272 for a healthy
  fasted participant, a ratio of 0.54 (123 ng/mL), which matches the text's
  statement that CL/F is about 85% higher in healthy fasted participants than
  in patients and the FDA review's table. The figure's value is close to what
  applying the fasted-F factor twice would give (0.686^2 / 1.272 = 0.37), but
  the maintainers could not confirm what the figure's simulation did. The
  model keeps the tabulated estimates. The other 17 rows agree within the
  figure's sampling and digitising error; the FDA review's "3.6-fold with 15
  mg QD" compares with 3.27-fold from Table S5 (F rises with dose by the
  exponent 0.0777, which the Figure 1 F percentages at 1 and 25 mg confirm),
  a gap within the sampling error of a ratio of two 500-participant medians.
- **No erratum** for Chang 2024 was found on Europe PMC or the journal site
  (checked 2026-10-31).
